title: Overnight Brown Butter Yeast Waffles
changes_from_base: Browned butter replaces melted butter, and instant yeast with a little bicarbonate replaces baking powder; the batter is chilled overnight (12-18 h), with no whisked whites.
summary: Yeasted waffles made with browned butter and left to ferment overnight, giving a deep flavour and a light, spongy batter.
equipment: wire rack set in a baking tray

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
neutral oil, for the iron (if needed)

steps.title: Brown
steps.text: Melt 85 g butter in a saucepan, stirring and scraping as it bubbles, and cook until golden brown.

steps.title: Stir
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in 20 g sugar, ½ tsp salt and 280 ml cold milk at once, then stir in 1 cold egg.

steps.title: Sift
steps.text: Sift in 210 g plain flour and stir until smooth, then stir in 4 g instant dried yeast and ¼ tsp bicarbonate of soda last.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cover and chill the batter overnight, 12-18 h, until gooey and spongy.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the waffle iron on medium until ready, brushing lightly with oil if using a cast-iron iron.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Pour in about a third of the batter for an 18 cm Belgian iron, or half for a 20 cm square iron, close and cook until golden brown but still steaming, 5-7 min.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Keep cooked waffles on a wire rack in a 90 °C oven while you cook the rest, then serve with maple syrup and sliced strawberries if you like.

tips: Stir the sugar, salt and milk into the browned butter straight away so it doesn't sit and catch in the hot pan.
Let the batter chill for the full 12-18 h, as the yeast needs that time to turn it gooey and spongy.
If your iron isn't non-stick, a light brush of oil before each waffle helps it release cleanly.
storage: Best eaten fresh and warm, straight from the iron. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
